A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AO-GPT study. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and can be matched despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original training comparisons, zero-shot perplexities, generation timings, architectural ablations, and generated samples.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds an experiment varying the left-to-right training mixture.

M1.justification: AO-GPT retains its target-position conditioning, adaptive LayerNorm, EMA, order-mixture training, context-order ensemble, and parallel sampling procedure. The additional mixing ratios test an existing strategy; moving the architecture description to Appendix A does not introduce a new method.

E1.justification: Both versions train on OpenWebText and evaluate on LAMBADA, WikiText2, PTB, WikiText103, and One Billion Words, alongside unconditional generation. The new mixing-ratio ablation retains the existing language-modeling tasks and data coverage.

E2.justification: The corresponding zero-shot comparisons retain GPT-2, sigma-GPT, SEDD, and RADD, and generation comparisons retain SEDD. Newly discussed CARD, WeDLM, and C2DLM are related work, not evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: v2 Figure 11 introduces 50% and 90% left-to-right mixtures alongside 10%. Also, v1 Figure 1 describes training losses, whereas its counterpart, v2 Figure 2, explicitly describes validation losses. This revises the reported measurement setting without establishing that the experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 Appendix B.2 adds a targeted sensitivity analysis comparing 10%, 50%, and 90% left-to-right mixtures. It extends v1's comparison of purely any-order training with a 10% mixture. Existing positional-encoding, EMA, fixed-order, and ensembling analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-training run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new ablation uses ordinary loss curves without introducing uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: New Figure 11 reports that increasing the left-to-right mixture lowers left-to-right loss but worsens any-order loss. The numerical entries in v1 Tables 1, 3, and 5 match v2 Tables 4, 2, and 5. Generation perplexities are presented at reduced decimal precision, without evidence of a new performance gain.

T1.justification: v2 Section 2.2 omits v1's separate O(T n) complexity statement for Monte Carlo estimation of encoder-only AO-AR loss. The objective equivalence, conditional-probability counts, entropy lower-bound argument, sampling lemma, and Appendix C proof otherwise remain mathematically unchanged.

C1.justification: Both versions claim to disentangle formulation from architecture, identify advantages of left-to-right structure, and demonstrate roughly 25-fold faster generation with comparable perplexity under appropriate annealing. The revised abstract emphasizes efficiency, but the central contributions and their scope remain intact.

C2.justification: v2 replaces v1's assertion that ensembling confirms the dominant cause of the perplexity gap with a diagnostic qualification and acknowledges its computational impracticality. Section 6 adds limitations concerning perplexity as a downstream proxy and untested infilling, editing, and constrained generation. The new mixture analysis also identifies a specialization trade-off.

D1.justification: v2 Figure 5 explicitly states that generation order is fixed before each decoding run, explaining KV-cache applicability. Section 5.2 clarifies that context-order ensembles are used only for designated perplexity evaluations, never generation. These are additional disclosures; model specifications, hardware, and code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds positioning against CARD, WeDLM, and C2DLM and expands the distinction from XLNet's target-prediction fraction. It removes references to Block Diffusion, Train for the Worst, Plan for the Best, and Argmax Flows. Most existing related-work discussion is retained.

P1.justification: The narrative is substantially reorganized: related work moves ahead of the comparative studies, the former Section 5 architecture discussion becomes Appendix A, and experimental details become Appendix B. The abstract is rewritten, an appendix roadmap is added, and the impact discussion moves into the main paper.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column main-text layout and extensively relocates and resizes displays. The architecture figures and medium-model benchmark table move to appendices, the combined positional-encoding/EMA ablation is split into separate figures, and a mixing-ratio figure is added. The introductory schematic gains a numbered caption.

improvement.justification: The new mixing-ratio ablation provides useful evidence about the limits of increasing left-to-right supervision. Clearer ensembling disclosures, more cautious causal interpretation, and explicit downstream limitations improve how readers can assess the findings. The core methods, benchmark results, and empirical coverage remain largely unchanged, so the overall gain is limited.
